clue.text: Dee, famous in another setting, is put to work

indicators.note: putting the letters in another setting means arranging them in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notable from the River Dee area is being given a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in another setting' rearranges the nine letters of DEE and FAMOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: To make use of something is to employ it, to set it working.

clue.text: Parts of Macaulay Culkin movie now found in China

indicators.note: the answer is a part taken from the run of letters in the actor's name

explanation.surface: Pieces of a Macaulay Culkin film turn up in China.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit at the start of 'Macaulay'; Macaulay Culkin is the child star of Home Alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Portuguese territory was handed back in 1999 and is now a special region of the People's Republic.

clue.text: Finish off the Todd-AO process

indicators.note: to process material is to work it over, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark about the Todd-AO widescreen film process being used up.
explanation.walkthrough: Todd-AO was a widescreen cinema format; 'process' as a verb rearranges THE and TODDAO.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing someone off means killing them, and the phrase is the idiom for that.

clue.text: Laundered cash finally restored without any publicity

indicators.note: the letters are put back together in a different form
finally picks the closing letter of the word cash

explanation.surface: Money that was laundered is quietly put back, with no fuss made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives H, the end of 'cash'; 'restored' rearranges it with LAUNDERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unheralded arrives with no announcement or fanfare beforehand.

clue.text: Properties in eastern Victoria perhaps the first to sell

parts.note: Victoria is one Australian state, an example of the word

indicators.note: the first letter of the word sell is taken

explanation.surface: Houses in the eastern part of Victoria are about to go on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals that Victoria is an example of the class, here an Australian state.
explanation.definitionFit: Estates are landed properties, large houses with their grounds.

clue.text: Finest hose initially made from this

definitions.text: Finest hose initially made from this

indicators.note: the answer is made from these letters rearranged
initially takes the opening letter of the word hose

explanation.surface: The best stockings are made of this mesh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives H from 'hose'; 'made from' rearranges it with FINEST; the whole clue also describes the material.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-mesh fabric is the classic material for fancy tights and stockings.

clue.text: Thumb a ride with 9

definitions.meaning: to get a lift from a passing driver by holding out a thumb
refers to the answer at 9 across, a snag or drawback

explanation.surface: Hitchhiking, with a reference to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: A hitch is a snag, just as a catch is the hidden drawback in a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchhiking is thumbing a ride, and a hitch is also a snag or drawback.

clue.text: The fellow has a right to 9

parts.note: the fellow is referred to as he

explanation.surface: A man is entitled to something given in another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'to 9' is a verb: to catch what someone says.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a remark is to hear it, picking up the words spoken.

clue.text: It isn't commonly seen as corruption

definitions.meaning: the dialect contraction of 'it ain't', how 'it isn't' is said in casual speech

explanation.surface: Something widely viewed as a form of corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' marks informal or dialect speech, giving the contraction 'tain't.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a trace of contamination, the corrupting stain of something bad.

clue.text: CNN hired a drunk with an impediment

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters staggering about into a new order

explanation.surface: A news network took on a drunkard who has a speech defect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges the letters of CNN HIRED A.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance is an obstacle, something that impedes progress.

clue.text: Nab Tom before church

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Grab Tom before he goes to church.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom is a male cat, not a person's name here.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab someone is to seize or capture them.

clue.text: A statesman sat back — a man in trouble

indicators.note: back means the word sat is read from its end
to trouble something is to disturb it, so these letters are stirred

explanation.surface: A politician sat down again, a man in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses SAT to TAS; 'trouble' rearranges A MAN IN to MANIAN. 'A statesman' is cryptic: one from an Australian state.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is an Australian state, so its native is literally a person of a state.

clue.text: 9 redundant workers finally replaced

indicators.note: the letters are put back in a different place
finally takes the last letter of the word workers

explanation.surface: Laid-off staff have finally been replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives S from 'workers'; 'replaced' rearranges it with REDUNDANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch someone's meaning is to grasp or comprehend it.

clue.text: A leading light in vermin turnaround

indicators.note: a turnaround means the word is read the other way

parts.note: rats are vermin

explanation.surface: A prominent figure in a reversal of a pest problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnaround' reverses RATS.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a celebrity, a person who leads in their field.

clue.text: Shipwreck leading to an oil discharge on a Caribbean island

indicators.note: leading to puts the first piece ahead of what follows
in a down clue, on places the first part above, so before, the next
wreck means the letters of ship are smashed into a new order
a discharge lets the letters spill out rearranged

explanation.surface: A wrecked ship spills oil off a West Indian island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wreck' rearranges SHIP to HISP and 'discharge' rearranges AN OIL to ANIOL; in a down clue 'on a' sets A beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: The island shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic carries this Spanish-era name.

clue.text: Rocks found in prospectors' sieves

definitions.meaning: a verb: sways gently to and fro, as a baby is soothed
rocking troughs used by gold miners to wash gravel

explanation.surface: Stones found in gold-panners' screens.
explanation.walkthrough: A miner's cradle is a box rocked to separate gold from gravel.
explanation.definitionFit: To cradle is to rock gently, and a cradle is a gold-washing trough rocked by prospectors.

clue.text: Old measurement brought up in change to tax

indicators.note: in puts the reversed piece inside the word change
in a down clue, brought up means the word is turned upward, read backwards

parts.note: an ell is an old unit of cloth length

explanation.surface: An old unit of measure is restored during a tax reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses ELL to LLE, which goes 'in' CHANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To tax someone with a fault is to confront or accuse them, to dispute their conduct.

clue.text: Yokel needs ten (about) to get set

indicators.note: ten goes about the bumpkin, enclosing him

parts.note: a hick is a country bumpkin

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin needs about ten minutes to get ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TEN round HICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauce or jelly that firms up becomes stiffer, which is setting.

clue.text: Troubled Ukraine protects holy tree

indicators.note: the rearranged word surrounds and guards the inner piece
troubled means the letters of Ukraine are disturbed

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, holy

explanation.surface: A war-torn Ukraine shelters a sacred tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troubled' rearranges UKRAINE to KAURINE, which 'protects' PI.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tall New Zealand conifer valued for timber and gum.

clue.text: Manage to get a letter from Greece to the woman

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
Eve, the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: Succeed in delivering a letter from Greece to a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the woman' points to Eve, the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve something is to manage it, bringing it off successfully.

clue.text: Running off unceremoniously with a mate

definitions.text: Running off unceremoniously with a mate

parts.words: Running off unceremoniously with a mate
parts.note: describes a couple sneaking off to marry with no proper wedding

explanation.surface: Fleeing in a hurry with a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unceremoniously' is literal: no wedding ceremony with the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloping is running away secretly to marry, skipping the formal ceremony.

clue.text: 9 covering, true to form

parts.note: a cap is a covering

indicators.note: true is shaped to form something new, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Something covering is faithful to its shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to form' rearranges TRUE to TURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a fugitive is to capture them.

clue.text: Blocked creek's first cleared of trees

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of creek

parts.note: logged land has had its timber felled

explanation.surface: A stream choked after the forest was felled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives C from 'creek's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clogged pipe or channel is obstructed, blocked up.

clue.text: Kelvin replaces a student in local 9

indicators.note: replaces swaps one piece of the word for another

parts.note: taken as written
A plus L, the learner abbreviation for a student
K is the symbol for the kelvin temperature unit

explanation.surface: A man named Kelvin takes a student's place at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaces' puts K where AL (A plus L, a learner) was in LOCAL; 'local' in Britain also means a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch on a door is a fastening, the same thing as a lock.

clue.text: Viper given to half of Cleo's 9

indicators.note: given to adds the snake after the first piece
half of takes the first two letters of the name Cleo

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A snake handed to Cleopatra, a nod to her death.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleopatra famously died from an asp's bite.
explanation.definitionFit: A clasp on a bag or necklace is a catch, a fastening.

clue.text: Contract 9

definitions.meaning: refers to the answer at 9 across, used here of catching an infection

explanation.surface: A short definition pair: an agreement and a reference to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' is a verb, as in contracting flu.
explanation.definitionFit: To go down with flu is to contract or catch it.

clue.text: Gunslinger goes without hesitation for the musician

indicators.note: goes without means a piece is dropped from the word

parts.note: a holster slings a gun at the hip, read whimsically as a gun-slinger
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A cowboy gunman moves without pausing for the composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunslinger' is cryptic for the leather case; 'goes without' drops ER. Gustav Holst wrote The Planets.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst was the English composer of The Planets suite.

clue.text: Prop is to remain

explanation.surface: A support is meant to stay in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a supporting prop or rope, and to stay is to remain.

clue.text: Nigh and night possibly very close

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: possibly suggests a different arrangement of night

explanation.surface: Near and night are almost the same word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape or close result is called by this phrase.

clue.text: Gold wreath's put back in the bay window

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: put back means the word is reversed

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian flower wreath

explanation.surface: A golden garland placed back in the window recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses LEI to IEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriel is a projecting upper-storey bay window.

clue.text: Blair's back, yet wandering around in vain

indicators.note: the rearranged word goes around the inner piece
wandering letters move into a new order
back means the title is read backwards

parts.note: Tony Blair was PM, the British prime minister

explanation.surface: Tony Blair returns, yet roams aimlessly to no avail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PM to MP; 'wandering' rearranges YET to ETY, which goes 'around' MP.
explanation.definitionFit: An empty gesture is one made in vain, hollow and futile.

clue.text: Sponsor prepared to give a lifetime guarantee?

definitions.text: Sponsor prepared to give a lifetime guarantee?

parts.words: Sponsor prepared to give a lifetime guarantee?
parts.note: describes a baptismal sponsor who vows lifelong spiritual care of a child

explanation.surface: A backer offering a guarantee for life.
explanation.walkthrough: At a christening the sponsor makes promises on the child's behalf for life.
explanation.definitionFit: This person stands sponsor at a baptism, pledging to guide the child.
